title: Eternal Ltd - 543320 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Eternal's Blinkit quick commerce guides long-term EBIT margin to top of range, now 6%, with Q1 flagged as peak competitive intensity.
summary.overview: Management spoke almost entirely to Blinkit (quick commerce), with questions also covering food delivery, Bistro, District, Nugget and payables. Management said competition is high but more predictable because it is now mostly subsidies on products and delivery fees, and that discount-led growth is unsustainable. Blinkit net order value (NOV) growth was described as robust, with NAOV expected to stay flat year on year. Management declined to guide Q2 volume growth, and said current EBIT margin is negative, so there is no ROCE yet. The call did not give reported quarterly financial figures beyond those cited in questions.

segments.name: Blinkit (quick commerce)
segments.commentary: Long-term margin now seen at the higher end of the range, given capex and efficiency gains. Q1 was called the peak of competitive intensity, and competition is now mainly subsidies on products and delivery fees. Management said non-metro growth is faster but partly reflects share shift from top-tier cities.

segments.name: Food delivery
segments.commentary: MTU growth is coming from both new users (acceleration over the last 3-4 quarters) and higher frequency. Management is price-competitive in markets where Toing and Ownly are spending aggressively, and says it is defending share. Monthly active restaurants dipped slightly due to the LPG disruption.

segments.name: Bistro
segments.commentary: Adding about 10 kitchens per quarter and expanding cautiously. Older kitchens are improving on throughput, menu pricing and operations. Bistro is in a separate entity, with no overlap in food delivery NOV or profit.

segments.name: District (going-out)
segments.commentary: Dining-out and movies are the largest categories, with retail stores and events the more promising newer ones. Customer base is smaller than food delivery or quick commerce, with fewer cities and higher NAOV.

segments.name: Nugget (enterprise AI)
segments.commentary: Management described it as in stealth mode with good traction. Losses rose on manpower, and no GPU spend was cited. More detail is to come in a couple of quarters.

guidance_outlook: Blinkit long-term margin is now expected at the higher end of the prior range, and the quick commerce long-term guidance was raised to 6% from 5-6%.
Long-term GAAP EBIT margin of about 4% for Blinkit, after ESOP and depreciation; adjusted EBITDA close to 6%.
Blinkit NAOV is expected to stay in the same range, and may rise again in Q3 on seasonality, but not meaningfully.
Management gave no guidance on Q2 Blinkit volume growth.
Management said no near-term margin pressure is expected, and margins should continue to improve as growth continues.
capex_capacity: Capex per store is now INR 2.5 crore (includes warehousing), vs INR 1 crore earlier; lumpy, and capex per store over 6-9 months is said to be below INR 2.5 crore.
About 200 Blinkit stores added in Q1, with quarterly capex around INR 700 crore.
Shifting to larger stores; new-format stores are cited at 2,100-2,200 orders per day, and existing stores are being upgraded to larger properties.
Bistro is adding about 10 kitchens per quarter, with more aggressive expansion planned later.
Management said NOV per store per day rose about 60% against the earlier assumption, versus about 150% for capex per store.
demand_pricing: Competitive intensity in Q1 was the peak seen so far; competitors are subsidising grocery and delivery fees, and management sees limited room to go deeper.
Blinkit NAOV is flat YoY. Management said mix, assortment and price matching drive NAOV, and it is not a focus metric.
Blinkit retention and cohort spend: older cohorts spend about 3x versus three years earlier, mostly through frequency; the figure covers the full cohort, including churned customers.
Blinkit growth is mostly from existing cities; non-metros are growing faster on a smaller base.
Quick commerce MTU pareto is much flatter than food delivery (top 15-18% of customers drive 80% of revenue in food delivery).
Management said the pricing-led strategy is not sustainable, and that discounting is less effective in quick commerce than in e-commerce due to limited shelf space in dark stores.

qa_highlights.question: Why raise the quick commerce long-term margin guidance to 6% amid competition?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said capex per store and efficiency gains, plus larger store sizes, give higher margin visibility, so the company expects to finish at the higher end of the earlier range.

qa_highlights.question: Is Q1 the peak of competitive intensity, and what does predictability mean?
qa_highlights.answer: Albinder Singh Dhindsa said Q1 was the peak seen to date because more players were aggressive. Competition now mainly takes the form of product and delivery-fee subsidies, which he said cannot go much deeper without large losses.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit AOV fall for two quarters, and will it recover?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the drop is in line with last year and mostly reflects category mix and price matching. NAOV is an outcome, flat YoY, and not expected to grow meaningfully. Q3 may rise on seasonality.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Blinkit contribution margin not rise with take rate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited higher minimum wages in several states and larger new stores with lower early contribution. Q1 last-mile costs are seasonally high, and YoY gross profit gains have largely flowed to contribution.

qa_highlights.question: Why is Blinkit capex around INR 700 crore for 200 stores when the stated capex per store is INR 2.5 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said warehouse capex is lumpy, so the per-store figure should be read over 6-9 months or longer. Over those periods capex per store is below INR 2.5 crore, and management expects that to continue.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the net working capital reduction to 14 days?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal said lower inventory days, from better replenishment and throughput, drove the cut from 18 to 14 days, with a steady-state target of 12 days. Kunal Swarup said the Q1 OCF lift came from a one-off tax refund on higher advance tax.

qa_highlights.question: What explains the slight dip in food delivery restaurant count?
qa_highlights.answer: Akshant Goyal attributed the dip to the LPG situation last quarter, which took some restaurants offline. He did not cite rationalisation.

risks_watch: Competition from Toing and Ownly in food delivery, and quick commerce subsidy intensity, which could put pressure on margins or MTU growth.
Q2 Blinkit volume trends, since no guidance was given; the analyst's historical 18-20% 1Q-to-2Q range was not addressed.
Blinkit contribution margin trajectory as store formats and minimum wages change; Q1 was described as seasonally weak.
Inventory losses held at about 1.8% of NOV, with management not expecting much improvement.
Capex intensity and ROCE: EBIT margin is currently negative, so there is no ROCE yet; management said the company will accept lower margins if ROCE holds.
Nugget losses (manpower-driven) and limited disclosure; Bistro is expanding cautiously, with unit economics still being proven.
Payables growth (about INR 1,650 crore QoQ increase) and whether terms with brands are improving; management said it is scale-driven.
summary.management_tone: Confident on Blinkit margins and competitive discipline, with management saying discounting is unsustainable and competition is now predictable. It was evasive on Q2 volumes, on ROCE today ("there's no ROCE") and on the capex-per-store comparison. It was cautious on Bistro and Nugget, which are at an early stage.
key_quotes: We are fundamentally a supply-creation business and if you channel your supply towards providing discounts to customers, then that's what the business becomes.
Over the longer term, the right metric to compare this with is Q1 of the previous year, and it could differ from quarter to quarter depending on seasonality.
The more we invest, even if the margins fall, as long as the ROCE remains high, the absolute dollar of profit on the business will be more.

adds.what: About 200 Blinkit dark stores added in Q1 FY27, shifting to larger new-format stores
Bistro kitchens, adding about 10 per quarter

growth.why: Management guided Blinkit's quick commerce long-term adjusted EBITDA margin to the high end of 6% (from 5-6%) and said NAOV will stay flat YoY, with no Q2 volume guidance; growth is backed by ~200 store additions in Q1 (~INR 700 crore quarterly capex) and a volume rise of 21% QoQ, but no revenue growth number was given.
